narrator.how: a man telling a parable: even, unhurried, a little grave, with the repetitions of a fairy tale read aloud; never sentimental

fisherman.how: a young fisherman: few words, plain and blunt, a little hoarse from the sea; when he is moved he loses his words and says one

soul.how: the Fisherman's own voice as he hears it inside him: almost a whisper, breathy and dry, close to the ear, lower and slower than his own; clever, exact and mocking — or, when she longs, tired

mermaid.how: a young girl of the sea: light, bright, laughing easily, singing a little as she talks; says strange human words as if tasting them

witch.how: a young red-haired witch: quick, low and teasing, laughing first; under the laugh, hurt

priest.how: an old priest who thunders from habit: deep, firm and certain, a pulpit voice even in a small room

potter.how: a widowed potter: kind, plain and tired, a few words at a time; when he is hurt, very quiet

widow.how: a fisherman's widow: low and even, asking nothing, every word weighed

girl.how: a village girl dancing barefoot at a feast: breathless, merry, calling out

women.how: village women whispering behind their hands: hushed, eager, a little afraid
